mainTopic: הלל after rain on a fast day, the end of the third perek, and the משנה on ברכת כהנים, the מעמדות, the wood-offering days, and the five tragedies of the summer fasts
overview: The amud opens by finishing a rule. If rain comes before midday on a fast day, people go home and eat first, because הלל is said only on a full stomach. The גמרא challenges this from a story where רב פפא had people say הלל first. It answers that the people of מחוזא were different, since they tended to get drunk. Then the third perek ends with a הדרן, and a new perek begins. Its משנה lists three times when כהנים bless four times in one day, and explains the מעמדות: groups who stood at the daily offering for all of ישראל, fasted Monday to Thursday, and read the Creation story each day. It lists which days some מעמד gatherings were skipped, where רבי עקיבא changes his version to follow בן עזאי. It also lists the nine family days for bringing wood to the מזבח. The amud ends as the משנה begins listing the five tragedies of שבעה עשר בתמוז and תשעה באב, a list that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: הלל is said only on a full stomach
steps.stepSummary: The text finishes the rule that the Great הלל is said only when people are full and satisfied.
steps.simpleTranslation: …only on a satisfied soul and a full stomach.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a rule from just before this text: if rain comes early on a fast day, people eat first and only then say הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that praise of thanks should be said in a relaxed, satisfied state, not while hungry from fasting. So the fast is stopped, people go home to eat, and they say הלל afterward.

keyTerms.meaning: A satisfied soul, a person who has eaten
A full stomach
Psalms of praise said as thanks, here for the rain

phrases.english: only on a satisfied soul
phrases.notes: This sentence starts on the previous amud: the Great הלל is only said when people are full like this.

phrases.english: and a full stomach.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא עַל נֶפֶשׁ שְׂבֵעָה וְכָרֵס מְלֵאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a statement that began before this text
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל for rain on a fast day is said only after eating, on a full stomach.

steps.title: רב פפא had them say הלל before eating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rule with a story where רב פפא told people to say הלל first and eat afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב פפא came to the synagogue of אבי גובר and declared a fast. Rain fell before midday, and he said to them: Say הלל, and afterward eat and drink!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the rule is really true, because רב פפא did the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule said to eat first and say הלל later. In רב פפא's case the rain also came before midday, yet he had them say הלל right away, while they were still fasting. That looks like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? This opens a challenge
Happened to come to a place
Declared a fast
Midday

phrases.english: Is that so?
But רב פפא happened to come
to the synagogue of אבי גובר
and he declared a fast,
and rain fell for them before midday,
and he said [to them: Say] הלל
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording. Without them, the line just says he said הלל.

phrases.english: and afterward eat and drink!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא רַב פָּפָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי כְּנִישְׁתָּא דַּאֲבִי גוֹבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule from step 1 with a story
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that people eat first and only then say הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב פפא, in the same situation, had them say הלל first and eat after, which goes against the rule.

steps.title: The people of מחוזא were different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב פפא's case was special, because the people of מחוזא often got drunk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The people of מחוזא are different, because drunkenness is common among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by showing that רב פפא's case was an exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule still stands: normally, eat first and then say הלל. In מחוזא, if people went home to eat and drink, they might get drunk and not come back to say הלל properly. So רב פפא had them say it first.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different; a special case
A Babylonian city, home of אבי גובר's synagogue
Drunkenness

steps.whatToRemember: The general rule stays: eat first, then say הלל. רב פפא's story was a local exception for a city where people tended to get drunk.

phrases.english: The people of מחוזא are different,
phrases.notes: The synagogue of אבי גובר was in מחוזא, which is why the answer talks about its people.

phrases.english: because drunkenness is common among them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי בְּנֵי מָחוֹזָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 2
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a local exception
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב פפא's story seemed to show that הלל comes before eating.
steps.terutzMaskana: Normally people eat first. In מחוזא, people said הלל first so drinking would not stop them from saying it.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing סדר תעניות אלו
steps.stepSummary: The third perek of מסכת תענית ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, perek סדר תעניות אלו.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line for the perek that just ended.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying הדרן shows love for the learning and the hope of coming back to it. It marks a clear break before the new perek starts.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; said when finishing a perek

phrases.english: We will return to you, סדר תעניות אלו

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַרַן עֲלָךְ סֵדֶר תַּעֲנִיּוֹת אֵלּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the perek that ended in step 3
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The third perek of תענית is complete.

steps.title: Three times a year כהנים bless four times in one day
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה lists three occasions when כהנים do נשיאת כפים in all four תפילות of the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: At three times in the year, כהנים raise their hands four times in a day: at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילת שערים. These are fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The new perek opens with a משנה listing the days when ברכת כהנים is said in four תפילות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually there are not four תפילות in a day. On these three occasions there is also a נעילה תפילה, so the כהנים bless at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: Times or occasions
Raise their hands; the כהנים saying ברכת כהנים
The closing of the gates; the נעילה תפילה
Groups of people who stood by the daily offerings for all of כלל ישראל

phrases.english: At three times in the year
priests raise their hands
four times in the day;
at the morning prayer, at the additional prayer, at the afternoon prayer,
and at the closing of the gates:
on fast days, and during the מעמדות,
and on יום הכפורים.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה פְּרָקִים בְּשָׁנָה כֹּהֲנִים נוֹשְׂאִין אֶת כַּפֵּיהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the new perek after the הדרן
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On fast days, מעמדות, and יום הכפורים, כהנים do נשיאת כפים at שחרית, מוסף, מנחה, and נעילה.

steps.title: The source for the מעמדות
steps.stepSummary: The משנה starts explaining the מעמדות by quoting a פסוק about the daily offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: These are the מעמדות. Since it says: "Command the children of Israel… My offering, My food."
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins explaining what the מעמדות are. It is setting up a question by first bringing a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק tells all of כלל ישראל to bring God's offering. This shows that the daily offering belongs to the whole nation, not only to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Command
My offering, My food; the daily offering

phrases.english: These are the מעמדות.
Since it is stated:
"Command the children of Israel
My offering, My food,"

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵלּוּ הֵן מַעֲמָדוֹת. לְפִי שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the term מעמדות mentioned in step 5
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daily offering is commanded to all of בני ישראל, so it belongs to everyone.

steps.title: How can an offering be brought without its owner there?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how the offering of all Israel can be brought when they are not standing next to it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But how can a person's offering be brought when he is not standing by it?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה raises a problem that sets up its answer, which comes next: the system of מעמדות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the daily offering belongs to every Jew, then every Jew should be present when it is brought. Since the whole nation cannot be in the בית המקדש every day, there must be some arrangement, and that is the reason for the מעמדות.

keyTerms.meaning: How
Standing by it, present at the offering

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a challenge against the משנה. The משנה asks this question itself to explain why the מעמדות were needed.

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי הֵיאַךְ קׇרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קָרֵב
phrases.english: But how can a person's offering be sacrificed
when he is not standing by it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי הֵיאַךְ קׇרְבָּנוֹ שֶׁל אָדָם קָרֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a practical problem that comes from the פסוק in step 6
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the whole nation can count as present at its own daily offering

steps.title: The early prophets set up 24 watches, each with a standing group
steps.stepSummary: The משנה answers how all of ישראל can be part of the daily offering: the נביאים הראשונים created 24 משמרות, and each had a מעמד of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The early prophets set up twenty-four watches. For each watch there was a standing group in ירושלים made up of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question from step 7. Representatives stood at the offering on behalf of all of ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The problem was that a קרבן belonging to all of ישראל needs its owners to be present, and the whole nation cannot stand there. The solution is a system of representatives. The people are split into 24 groups, and each group has a מעמד that stands for the whole nation during its turn.

keyTerms.meaning: The early prophets
Watches: the 24 rotating groups that took turns serving in the בית המקדש
Literally 'standing'; the group of representatives who stood for all of ישראל during the offering

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the base of everything that follows. All the fasts and readings in the coming steps are what the members of the מעמד did.

phrases.english: The early prophets instituted
twenty-four watches.
For each and every watch
there was a standing group in Jerusalem
phrases.notes: A מעמד is a group of people who 'stand' at the offering for everyone else, like stand-ins for the whole nation.

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁל כֹּהֲנִים שֶׁל לְוִיִּם וְשֶׁל יִשְׂרְאֵלִים.
phrases.english: of priests, of Levites, and of Israelites.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִתְקִינוּ נְבִיאִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים עֶשְׂרִים וְאַרְבָּעָה מִשְׁמָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question asked in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A system of 24 משמרות, each with a representative מעמד of כהנים, לוים and ישראלים, lets all of ישראל be represented at the offering.

steps.title: What happened when a watch's turn came
steps.stepSummary: When a watch's turn came, its כהנים and לוים went up to ירושלים. The Israelites of that watch gathered in their own towns and read מעשה בראשית.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it was time for the watch to go up, the כהנים and לוים went up to ירושלים. The ישראלים of that watch gathered in their towns and read the story of Creation.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה describes what each part of the watch did during its week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כהנים and לוים do the actual service in ירושלים. The Israelites of that watch take part from home by gathering together and reading the Torah's account of Creation.

keyTerms.meaning: To go up (to ירושלים)
They gather together
The account of Creation (בראשית chapter 1 to 2:3)

phrases.english: When the time came for the watch to go up,
the priests and Levites go up to Jerusalem,
and the Israelites of that watch
gather in their towns,
and read the account of Creation.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִגִּיעַ זְמַן הַמִּשְׁמָר לַעֲלוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the watch system from step 8 worked in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כהנים and לוים go up to serve; the ישראלים of the watch gather in their towns and read מעשה בראשית.

steps.title: The מעמד fasted Monday to Thursday, but not Friday or Sunday
steps.stepSummary: The members of the מעמד fasted four days, from Monday through Thursday. They did not fast on Friday out of respect for שבת. They did not fast on Sunday, so they would not go straight from rest to hardship and become dangerously weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: The members of the מעמד fasted four days a week, Monday to Thursday. They did not fast on Friday, out of respect for שבת. They did not fast on Sunday, so they would not go straight from rest and enjoyment to effort and fasting, and die.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה tells us which days the מעמד fasted, and gives a reason for each day they skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate reasons. Friday is skipped so that people do not start שבת hungry. Sunday is skipped because a sudden switch from שבת's rest and pleasure to fasting could be dangerous to their health.

keyTerms.meaning: They fast
Friday (the day before שבת)
Sunday (the first day of the week)
Delight, enjoyment

steps.confusionAlert: Here בְּשַׁבָּת does not mean 'on שבת'. In the phrase אֶחָד בְּשַׁבָּת, the word שבת means 'the week', so the phrase means Sunday.

phrases.english: And the members of the standing group would fast
four days a week,
from Monday until Thursday.
And they would not fast on Friday,
out of respect for Shabbat,
and not on Sunday,
so that they would not go from rest and delight
to hard effort and fasting, and die.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַנְשֵׁי הַמַּעֲמָד הָיוּ מִתְעַנִּין אַרְבָּעָה יָמִים בַּשָּׁבוּעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second practice of the מעמד: fasting during their week.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מעמד fasts Monday to Thursday. Friday is skipped for כבוד שבת, and Sunday is skipped to avoid a dangerous sudden change.

steps.title: Which part of the Creation story was read each day
steps.stepSummary: The משנה gives the daily reading schedule. Each day they read that day's part of Creation together with the start of the next day's part, ending with ויכלו on Friday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Sunday: 'In the beginning' and 'Let there be a firmament.' Monday: 'Let there be a firmament' and 'Let the waters gather.' Tuesday: 'Let the waters gather' and 'Let there be lights.' Wednesday: 'Let there be lights' and 'Let the waters swarm.' Thursday: 'Let the waters swarm' and 'Let the earth bring forth.' Friday: 'Let the earth bring forth' and 'The heavens were finished.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists exactly which section of מעשה בראשית the מעמד read on each day of the week.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each day has two sections. The second section of one day becomes the first section of the next day. This pattern moves the reading step by step through the whole Creation story over the week.

keyTerms.meaning: Firmament, sky
Let the waters be gathered
Lights (the sun, moon and stars)
And they were finished (בראשית 2:1)

phrases.english: On Sunday: 'In the beginning,' and 'Let there be a firmament.'
phrases.notes: Each name is the opening words of a section in בראשית 1. Notice how each day's second section repeats as the next day's first.

phrases.english: On Monday: 'Let there be a firmament,' and 'Let the waters be gathered.'
On Tuesday: 'Let the waters be gathered,' and 'Let there be lights.'
On Wednesday: 'Let there be lights,' and 'Let the waters swarm.'
On Thursday: 'Let the waters swarm,' and 'Let the earth bring forth.'
On Friday: 'Let the earth bring forth,' and 'The heavens were finished.'

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּיּוֹם הָרִאשׁוֹן: בְּרֵאשִׁית, וִיהִי רָקִיעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the details of the מעשה בראשית reading mentioned in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each day's reading is that day's part of Creation plus the next day's part. Friday ends with ויכלו.

steps.title: How and when the readings were done
steps.stepSummary: A long section was read by two people and a short one by one person. They read from the Torah at שחרית and מוסף. At מנחה they read by heart like קריאת שמע. On Friday at מנחה they did not gather at all, out of respect for שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A long section is read by two people, and a short one by one person. This is at שחרית and at מוסף. At מנחה they go in and read by heart, the way people say שמע. On Friday at מנחה they did not go in, out of respect for שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes describing the readings: how many readers there were, and at which תפילות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two kinds of reading. At שחרית and מוסף the section is read publicly from the Torah, split between readers according to its length. At מנחה it is only said by heart. On Friday afternoon even that is dropped, so people can get ready for שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: A section of the Torah
The morning תפילה
The additional תפילה
By heart (literally, 'by their mouths')

steps.whatToRemember: The מעמד stood in for all of ישראל. The כהנים and לוים served in ירושלים, while the Israelites of the watch gathered at home, fasted Monday to Thursday, and read the Creation story each day. They read from the Torah at שחרית and מוסף and by heart at מנחה, and stopped on Friday afternoon for כבוד שבת.

phrases.english: A long section is read by two people,
and the short one by a single person.
This is at the morning prayer and at the additional prayer.
And at the afternoon prayer they go in

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹרִין עַל פִּיהֶן, כְּקוֹרִין אֶת שְׁמַע.
phrases.english: and read it by heart, the way one recites Shema.

phrases.aramaic: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת בַּמִּנְחָה לֹא הָיוּ נִכְנָסִין —
phrases.english: On Friday at the afternoon prayer they would not go in,
out of respect for Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: פָּרָשָׁה גְּדוֹלָה קוֹרִין אוֹתָהּ בִּשְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how the daily sections from step 11 were read and at which times.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Long section: two readers; short section: one reader. From the Torah at שחרית and מוסף; by heart at מנחה. No gathering at מנחה on ערב שבת.

steps.title: Special days when the מעמד did not gather
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא teaches that on a day with הלל there is no מעמד at שחרית, on a day with קרבן מוסף none at נעילה, and on a day with קרבן עצים none at מנחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: On any day when הלל is said, the מעמד does not gather at שחרית. On a day with a קרבן מוסף, it does not gather at נעילה. On a day with a wood offering, it does not gather at מנחה. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists three kinds of special days, and for each one it tells us which of the מעמד's gatherings was skipped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 described the מעמד's regular gatherings. Now the משנה adds exceptions: on special days, certain gatherings were skipped. The ruling is credited to רבי עקיבא, which sets up a different version in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Praise from תהלים said on holidays and ראש חודש
The group of ישראלים connected to the watch on duty that week
The extra offering brought on שבת, holidays and ראש חודש
A donation of wood for the fire on the מזבח
A closing prayer said near the end of the day

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the מעמד was cancelled for the whole day. Particular gatherings were skipped, and not always only one. On a day with a קרבן מוסף, two are omitted: by one reading נעילה and the מנחה next to it, by another the מוסף's own gathering and נעילה.

phrases.english: Any day on which הלל is said:
there is no מעמד gathering at שחרית;
a day with an additional offering: there is none at נעילה;
phrases.notes: Here נעילה is a closing prayer near sunset on these days, not only the one on יום כיפור.

phrases.english: a day with a wood offering: there is none at מנחה.
These are the words of רבי עקיבא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל יוֹם שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ הַלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds exceptions to the regular schedule of מעמד gatherings given in step 12.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל day: no מעמד at שחרית. מוסף day: none at נעילה. Wood offering day: none at מנחה (according to רבי עקיבא).

steps.title: בן עזאי reports a different version from רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: בן עזאי tells רבי עקיבא that רבי יהושע taught it differently: a מוסף day has no מעמד at מנחה, and a wood offering day has none at נעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בן עזאי said to him: this is how רבי יהושע used to teach it. On a day with a קרבן מוסף, there is no מעמד at מנחה. On a day with a wood offering, there is none at נעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: בן עזאי challenges רבי עקיבא's version by quoting what he heard from רבי יהושע, which swaps two of the rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הלל rule is not disputed. Only the second and third rules are reversed: רבי עקיבא put מוסף with נעילה and wood with מנחה, while רבי יהושע put מוסף with מנחה and wood with נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: This is how he used to teach it

phrases.english: בן עזאי said to him:
This is how רבי יהושע used to teach it:
a day with an additional offering: there is no מעמד at מנחה;
a day with a wood offering: there is none at נעילה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ בֶּן עַזַּאי, כָּךְ הָיָה רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ שׁוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי עקיבא's version from step 13 with a tradition from רבי יהושע.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's pairing of מוסף with נעילה and wood offering with מנחה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A received teaching from רבי יהושע gives the reverse pairing, so רבי עקיבא's version does not match the tradition.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא accepts בן עזאי's version
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא changed his teaching to follow בן עזאי's version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא went back and began to teach it like בן עזאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא accepts the challenge and changes his own teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because בן עזאי's version came from רבי יהושע, רבי עקיבא gave up his own version. So the final rule is: מוסף day, no מעמד at מנחה; wood offering day, no מעמד at נעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: He went back on his earlier view, he changed his mind
To teach in line with someone else's version

steps.whatToRemember: Final version: הלל day, no מעמד at שחרית. מוסף day, none at מנחה. Wood offering day, none at נעילה.

phrases.english: רבי עקיבא went back on his view
and began to teach it like בן עזאי.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לִהְיוֹת שׁוֹנֶה כְּבֶן עַזַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the challenge from step 14 in favor of בן עזאי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The משנה follows רבי יהושע's version as reported by בן עזאי.

steps.title: The family days for donating wood
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says there were nine set days when priests and people brought wood, and begins listing the families and dates.
steps.simpleTranslation: There were nine set times for the wood offering of the כהנים and the people. On א׳ ניסן, the family of ארח בן יהודה. On כ׳ תמוז, the family of דוד בן יהודה. On ה׳ אב, the family of פרעוש בן יהודה. On ז׳ אב, the family of יונדב בן רכב. On י׳ אב, the family of סנאה בן בנימין. On ט״ו אב, the family of זתוא בן יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains what the 'wood offering' days from the previous steps were, and starts listing which family brought wood on which date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 13–15 mentioned the קרבן עצים without explaining it. Now we learn these were set days for particular families. The משנה says there were nine, but only six are listed here; the list continues after the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: The wood donated by כהנים and the people for the מזבח
Set time
The descendants of, the family of
In it, meaning in the same month

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה says 'nine' but you only see six here. The other dates come right after the next line, so nothing is missing.

phrases.english: The times for the wood of the priests and the people are nine:

phrases.aramaic: בְּאֶחָד בְּנִיסָן בְּנֵי אָרַח בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: on the first of Nisan, the descendants of Arach ben Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֶשְׂרִים בְּתַמּוּז בְּנֵי דָוִד בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: on the twentieth of Tammuz, the descendants of David ben Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה בְּאָב בְּנֵי פַרְעוֹשׁ בֶּן יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: on the fifth of Av, the descendants of Parosh ben Yehuda;

phrases.aramaic: בְּשִׁבְעָה בּוֹ בְּנֵי יוֹנָדָב בֶּן רֵכָב,
phrases.english: on the seventh of it [Av], the descendants of Yonadav ben Rechav;

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲשָׂרָה בּוֹ בְּנֵי סְנָאָה בֶּן בִּנְיָמִין,
phrases.english: on the tenth of it [Av], the descendants of Sena'a ben Binyamin;

phrases.aramaic: בַּחֲמִשָּׁה עָשָׂר בּוֹ בְּנֵי זַתּוּא בֶּן יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: on the fifteenth of it [Av], the descendants of Zattu ben Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְמַן עֲצֵי כֹהֲנִים וְהָעָם, תִּשְׁעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the wood offering days mentioned in steps 13–15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There were nine set family days for donating wood, starting with א׳ ניסן and including several days in אב.

steps.title: Other groups who joined on ט״ו אב
steps.stepSummary: Along with the family of זתוא בן יהודה came כהנים, לוים, people unsure of their tribe, and two special groups.
steps.simpleTranslation: With them came כהנים and לוים, anyone who was unsure which tribe he belonged to, the descendants of those who fooled others with a pestle, and the descendants of those who packed dried figs.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה pauses its list to say who else brought wood on ט״ו אב together with the family of זתוא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ט״ו אב was a bigger day than the others, because many groups joined in. The משנה names two groups by odd nicknames without explaining them; the גמרא will explain them later.

keyTerms.meaning: Was unsure or mistaken about which tribe he came from
Literally 'pestle stealers'; a group the גמרא explains later
Packers of dried figs; another group the גמרא explains later

phrases.english: And with them were priests and Levites,
and anyone who was unsure of his tribe,
and the descendants of those who fooled others with a pestle,
and the descendants of those who packed dried figs.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעִמָּהֶם כֹּהֲנִים וּלְוִיִּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds detail to the last date in step 16 (ט״ו אב, the family of זתוא בן יהודה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On ט״ו אב, כהנים, לוים, people unsure of their tribe, and two other named groups joined the family of זתוא in bringing wood.

steps.title: The last three wood-offering days
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list: the family of פחת מואב on the twentieth of אב, the family of עדין on the twentieth of אלול, and the family of פרעוש a second time on א׳ בטבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the twentieth of that month (אב), the family of פחת מואב son of יהודה brought wood. On the twentieth of אלול, the family of עדין son of יהודה did. On the first of טבת, the family of פרעוש brought wood a second time.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing the list of nine wood-offering days that it began earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are the final three entries in the list. The family of פרעוש already appeared earlier in the list, so this is their second turn. That is why the משנה says שבו, 'they came back.'

keyTerms.meaning: Name of a family from the tribe of יהודה
Name of another family from יהודה
A family that had two turns to bring wood
They came back, did it again
A second time

phrases.english: On the twentieth of it
phrases.notes: 'Of it' means the month of אב, the month named in the entries just before this.

phrases.english: the sons of פחת מואב son of יהודה;
on the twentieth of אלול
the sons of עדין son of יהודה;
on the first of טבת
the sons of פרעוש returned a second time.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעֶשְׂרִים בּוֹ בְּנֵי פַּחַת מוֹאָב בֶּן יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of wood-offering families and dates begun in Step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The final wood-offering days are 20 אב (פחת מואב), 20 אלול (עדין), and 1 טבת (פרעוש, second time).

steps.title: Why the first of טבת had no מעמד
steps.stepSummary: On א׳ בטבת there was no מעמד at all, because that day had הלל, a קרבן מוסף, and a קרבן עצים.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the first of טבת there was no מעמד, because on that day there was הלל, a קרבן מוסף, and a קרבן עצים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה applies the earlier rule about when the מעמד is cancelled to the special day of א׳ בטבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier we learned that each of these three things (הלל, מוסף, wood offering) cancels the מעמד at one of the day's prayer times. On א׳ בטבת all three happen together, and the משנה concludes that there was no מעמד that day. This holds under either version from Steps 13-15, since all three features are present.

keyTerms.meaning: The first day of the month of טבת
The start of a new month, a day with a קרבן מוסף
The festival that falls on this date, when הלל is said

steps.whatToRemember: When a day has הלל, מוסף, and a wood offering all at once, the מעמד is cancelled for the whole day.

phrases.english: On the first of טבת
there was no מעמד on it,
because there was הלל on it
phrases.notes: הלל is said because this day falls during חנוכה.

phrases.english: and a קרבן מוסף
phrases.notes: It is ראש חודש, which has a מוסף.

phrases.english: and a wood offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּאֶחָד בְּטֵבֵת לֹא הָיָה בּוֹ מַעֲמָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the date just listed in Step 18 and applies the מעמד-cancelling rule from Steps 13-15 to it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On א׳ בטבת there is no מעמד at all, since it has הלל, מוסף, and a wood offering.

steps.title: Five tragedies on each of two dates
steps.stepSummary: A new section of the משנה opens: five tragedies happened to our ancestors on שבעה עשר בתמוז and five on תשעה באב. It starts listing the ones of שבעה עשר בתמוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: Five things happened to our ancestors on the seventeenth of תמוז, and five on the ninth of אב. On the seventeenth of תמוז...
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new topic, the two big fast days of summer. It is setting up a list, and the list itself continues in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line gives the headline: two dates, five tragedies each. The last words start the detailed list for שבעה עשר בתמוז, which the משנה goes on to spell out next.

keyTerms.meaning: Happened, came upon (used here for bad events)
Our ancestors
The seventeenth of תמוז, a fast day
The ninth of אב, a fast day

phrases.english: Five things happened
to our ancestors
on the seventeenth of תמוז,
and five on the ninth of אב.
On the seventeenth of תמוז

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲמִשָּׁה דְּבָרִים אֵירְעוּ אֶת אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בְּשִׁבְעָה עָשָׂר בְּתַמּוּז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the topic of wood offerings and מעמדות and opens a new משנה topic about the summer fast days.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Five tragedies occurred on שבעה עשר בתמוז and five on תשעה באב; the list for שבעה עשר בתמוז begins.
